findings.reason: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: UDP-tunnel GSO super-packets reaching skb_udp_tunnel_segment() (called from udp4_tunnel_gso_segment/udp6 paths in net/ipv4/udp_offload.c:644 and the fou/geneve/vxlan tunnel gso chains); the outer UDP header bytes at skb_transport_header (uh->len, uh->check) are packet-supplied, attacker-influenced for any tunneled traffic forwarded or terminated by the host (vxlan/geneve/fou egress through software GSO). VIOLATED INVARIANT: uh is captured at line 181 as struct udphdr *uh = udp_hdr(skb), a raw pointer into skb->head, and must be refetched after any call that can reallocate the head. pskb_may_pull(skb, tnl_hlen) at line 189, where tnl_hlen = skb_inner_mac_header(skb) - skb_transport_header(skb) spans the region that includes the outer UDP header itself, calls __pskb_pull_tail() (net/core/skbuff.c) which for a cloned/non-linear skb invokes pskb_expand_head() and frees/replaces skb->head, invalidating every pre-call pointer into the head - the exact head-relocation invariant broken in the seed's pep_get_sb(). No refetch occurs between the pull and the uses. UNSAFE USE: the stale pre-pull uh is dereferenced at line 199 (partial = (__force __wsum)uh->len) and line 202 (partial = csum_sub(csum_unfold(uh->check), partial)) to compute the 'partial' checksum delta; that value is later written into every segmented packet's UDP checksum at line 292 (uh->check = ~csum_fold(csum_add(partial, htonl(len)))) - transmitted packet bytes (kernel state) derived from reads through potentially freed slab memory, a KASAN-detectable slab use-after-free read on the GSO segmentation path. The next refetch is only at line 275 (uh = udp_hdr(skb)) inside the per-segment loop, after gso_inner_segment has already run, i.e. far too late for the reads at 199-202. COUNTEREVIDENCE: if the tunnel GSO skb is fully linear and uncloned (the common case for locally generated tunnel skbs), pskb_may_pull is a no-op and the pointer stays valid, so the UAF requires a non-linear or cloned UDP-tunnel GSO skb (e.g. forwarded tunneled traffic with frags or frag-list reaching software segmentation); no runtime KASAN reproducer was produced; the stale reads feed only the checksum constant, limiting impact to checksum corruption of transmitted segments and freed-memory information disclosure into them rather than arbitrary write. Note the parallel gro branch for s01 (fact f008) reported the identical unpatched pattern in that snapshot's copy of this function; the s04 copy retains it.

candidates.reason: __skb_udp_tunnel_segment(): uh captured at 181 via udp_hdr(skb); pskb_may_pull(skb, tnl_hlen) at 189 may __pskb_pull_tail -> pskb_expand_head and free skb->head; stale uh->len read at 199 and uh->check read at 202 with no refetch (next refetch only at 275 after segmentation); stale-derived 'partial' written into every segment's uh->check at 292. Raised as the finding.

tcp_gro_pull_header() captures th = skb_gro_header(skb, hlen, off) and, when the header needs more data (skb_gro_may_pull fails at off+thlen), explicitly refetches th = skb_gro_header_slow(skb, hlen, off) and returns the fresh pointer; both callers (net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c:429, net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c:56) use the returned post-pull pointer only. No stale dereference.

napi_frags_skb(): after gro_pull_from_frag0(skb, hlen) (which memcpys frag0 data into the head tail and advances/adjusts NAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->frag0 and frag0_len), the frag0 cursor is explicitly advanced (frag0 += hlen; frag0_len -= hlen) before __skb_pull(skb, hlen); dev_gro_receive's gro_try_pull_from_frag0(skb) (lines 554, 573) runs after the protocol handlers return and before the skb is added to the gro list, so no frag0-derived header pointer held by a handler survives it. Frag-list bookkeeping is updated, not left stale.

tcp4_gro_receive(): th comes from tcp_gro_pull_header(skb) which refetches through skb_gro_header_slow when needed; th2 = tcp_hdr(p) points into the held GRO packet p (not the pulled skb); the post-merge write tcp_flag_word(th2) at 348 also targets p. No pointer into skb->head of the incoming skb is used after a relocating call.

tcp6_gro_receive(): identical tcp_gro_pull_header discipline; tcp6_check_fraglist_gro() re-derives hdr = skb_gro_network_header(skb) fresh (line 34) and th is the post-pull pointer passed in. No stale dereference.

ipv6_gro_receive(): iph captured at 218 via skb_gro_header; when exthdrs must be walked, ipv6_gro_pull_exthdrs() (line 229) internally refetches opth via skb_gro_header(skb, off + len, off) after each length-driven pull (lines 40, 46), and the caller refetches iph = skb_gro_network_header(skb) at line 235 before the same-flow comparisons at 254-275; the GSO twin ipv6_gso_pull_exthdrs() refetches opth = (void *)skb->data after each pskb_may_pull (lines 77, 83). Correct refetch discipline.

inet_gro_receive(): iph captured at 1484 via skb_gro_header(skb, hlen, off) (which itself goes through skb_gro_header_slow when needed); all iph dereferences (protocol at 1488, 0x45 check 1494, fragment check 1497, csum 1500, flush computation 1504, same-flow compare 1518-1520) precede the offset-only skb_gro_pull(skb, sizeof(*iph)) at 1532, which does not touch the head buffer. No stale use.

gre_gro_receive(): greh captured at 141 via skb_gro_header; when grehlen (key/csum options) requires more data, skb_gro_may_pull fails and greh is explicitly refetched via greh = skb_gro_header_slow(skb, hlen, off) at line 178 before the flag checks and the same-flow comparisons (206-219); grohlen-based skb_gro_pull at 222 happens after the last greh dereference. Correct pattern.

gue_gro_receive(): guehdr captured at 349 via skb_gro_header; when optlen (guehdr->hlen << 2, attacker-controlled) requires more data, guehdr is refetched via guehdr = skb_gro_header_slow(skb, len, off) at 376; the remcsum path reassigns guehdr from skb_gro_remcsum_process() (gro.h:332) which internally re-fetches via skb_gro_header(skb, off + plen, off) after its pull and returns the fresh pointer; data is re-derived from &guehdr[1] after each reassignment (392, 408). The non-GRO twin gue_udp_recv documents 'guehdr may change after pull' (line 174) and refetches. Correct discipline.

geneve_gro_receive(): gh captured at 882; refetched at 893 via skb_gro_header_slow when the option-extended gh_len requires it; when a GRO hint is present the code pulls the hinted nested headers and refetches again gh = skb_gro_header(skb, off_gnv + gh_len, off_gnv) at 907 before geneve_opt_gro_hint()/geneve_hdr_match()/geneve_opt_gro_hint_validate_csum() dereference it; the RX decap twin geneve_post_decap_hint() also refetches *geneveh = geneve_hdr(skb) after its pskb_may_pull (lines 588-592). Correct refetch discipline on both paths.

udp_gro_receive_segment(): uh = udp_gro_udphdr(skb) at 697 is read (check 706, len 712, port compare 727, gro_receive_network_flush 737) before the only pskb_may_pull at 749, which sits in the is_flist branch; after that pull the code never dereferences uh again on that branch (the skb_gro_postpull_rcsum(skb, uh, ...) at 761 is in the non-flist else-branch where no pull ran), and uh2 = udp_hdr(p) points into the held GRO packet p whose head is not relocated by pulling skb. No stale dereference.

vxlan_gro_receive()/vxlan_gpe_gro_receive() are thin wrappers that immediately delegate to eth_gro_receive/ptype->callbacks.gro_receive without capturing or holding any header pointer across a relocating call; vxlan_gro_prepare-style remcsum handling refetches through skb_gro_remcsum_process which returns the fresh pointer. No stale pointer surface.

limitations: All conclusions are static source-analysis results on snapshots/s04: no runtime reproducer, KASAN trace, or build was produced; the reported __skb_udp_tunnel_segment finding requires the UDP-tunnel GSO skb to actually be cloned or non-linear at the transport-to-inner-MAC region so pskb_may_pull -> __pskb_pull_tail -> pskb_expand_head really frees the old head, which is driver/GRO/forwarding-path dependent and was not dynamically demonstrated.

The audit deeply read the GRO/GSO core and the main protocol/tunnel handlers (net/core/gro.c, include/net/gro.h, net/ipv4/{tcp,udp,gre,fou}_offload.c, net/ipv4/af_inet.c, net/ipv6/{ip6,tcpv6,udp}_offload.c, drivers/net/{geneve.c,vxlan/vxlan_core.c}); other *_gro_receive/_gso_segment files matched by grep (net/sctp/offload.c, net/ipv4/esp4_offload.c, net/ipv6/esp6_offload.c, net/mpls/mpls_gso.c, net/nsh/nsh.c, net/xfrm/xfrm_iptfs.c, and ~30 drivers/ files such as stmmac, sunvnet_common, niu, ipoib, t7xx, netvsc) were only pattern-screened, not line-by-line audited, within the twelve-candidate triage bound.

GRO implementations living inside individual NIC drivers (drivers/net/ethernet/*/ gro callbacks beyond vxlan/geneve) were listed via grep but not deep-read; a driver-internal gro handler that caches a header pointer across its own pskb_may_pull/skb_gro_pull would be missed by this pass.

Whether upstream Linux has since fixed __skb_udp_tunnel_segment() could not be checked (no network or Git access); the finding reflects the source as present in snapshots/s04, and the parallel s01 gro branch (fact f008) independently reported the same unpatched shape in its snapshot, which supports but does not prove the s04 copy is also unfixed upstream.

The stale reads in the reported finding feed only the 'partial' checksum constant written into each segment's uh->check at line 292; the exact information-disclosure potential of freed-head bytes propagating into transmitted checksums was not quantified, and exploitation impact (checksum corruption vs info leak) remains a hypothesis.
